SLA Language Reference > Type System

Type System

This page introduces SLA's types: primitive types, legacy aliases, combined forms such as arrays/slices/tuples, the borrowing type &T, and type aliases combined with & (flat data layouts). After reading this page, you can choose the correct type spelling for function signatures and struct fields.

Primitive types

SLA's primitive types are defined inside the compiler (the Primitive enum in src/ast.zig) as:

CategoryTypes
Signed integersi8 i16 i32 i64 isize
Unsigned integersu8 u16 u32 u64 usize
Floating pointf32 f64
Otherbool, void, ptr (raw pointer)
Migration-period aliasesOld spellings such as int and float are still accepted (internally marked as legacy aliases)

Real examples (demos/rosetta/04_loop/main.sla and demo 314):

fn fill_zero(arr: [u8; 4]) -> [u8; 4] {
    arr.fill(0);
    return arr;
}

let data: ptr = PTR_NULL();   // 裸指针来自 sa_std 契约

Arrays, slices, and range indexing

Fixed-length arrays are written [T; N]; slice parameters are written &[T]; taking a sub-range of an array yields a slice. The two snippets below are from demos 13 / 14 / 44 respectively:

let values: [i32; 4] = [1, 2, 3, 4];
let window_sum: i32 = values[1..3].iter().sum();

fn sum(values: &[i32]) -> i32 {
    values.iter().copied().sum()
}
// 调用：sum(&values) —— 数组实参自动按“数组转切片借用”物化

Tuples

Tuple literals use parentheses, and fields are accessed by index:

let pair = (3, 4);
println("({}, {})", pair.0, pair.1);        // demos/rosetta/11_tuples

fn head(t: (i32, i32, i32)) -> i32 {
    return t.0;
}

Copy semantics of tuples: a tuple is a Copy type if and only if all of its elements are Copy (the per-element Copy judgment recurses layer by layer, with nested tuples expanded layer by layer). A fully Copy tuple is materialized as a by-value copy at let, const, assignment, and destructuring binding sites: the binding produces an independent new value, the source binding is not consumed and can still be read afterwards; destructuring bindings follow the same rule as ordinary let — the root of a Copy type is not consumed by destructuring. As soon as it contains one non-Copy element, the tuple as a whole is non-Copy: binding is a move, and reading the source after the move reports UseAfterMove. Tuples containing arrays keep move semantics (arrays do not participate in the Copy judgment), and reuse likewise reports UseAfterMove.

The borrowing type &T and dereference *

&T denotes a borrowing view. In the current version, &self/&T cover both read and write conventions, with the SA Referee judging read/write conflicts after lowering. Dereference uses the prefix *; the following is from demos/rosetta/102_raii_guard/main.sla:

fn inspect(counter: &Mutex<i32>, skip: bool) -> i32 {
    let guard = counter.lock().unwrap();
    if skip {
        let value = *guard;
        return value;
    };
    let current = *guard;
    let updated = current + 3;
    *guard = updated;
    return updated;
}

type aliases and & combination

type declares a type alias. The frontend recently added an alias form combined with &: the fields of multiple source types are flattened into one aggregate layout, used for ECS-style flat data components (demos/rosetta/313_type_alias_flattening/main.sla):

struct Transform { x: i32, y: i32 }
struct Velocity  { vx: i32, vy: i32 }

type BulletData = Transform & Velocity & { damage: i32 };

fn spawn_bullet() -> i32 {
    let bullet = BulletData { x: 10, y: 20, vx: 30, vy: 40, damage: 50 };
    return bullet.x + bullet.y + bullet.vx + bullet.vy + bullet.damage;
}
NoteBulletData { ... } is a real single struct layout, not runtime multiple inheritance. All fields are flattened into consecutive offsets at compile time.

Generic types

Structs and enums can carry type parameters, instantiated at use sites. SLA uses compile-time monomorphization: each combination of type arguments generates an independent layout and strongly typed functions, introducing no runtime dispatch (demos/rosetta/10_generics_monomorph/main.sla):

struct OptionValue<T> {
    is_some: bool,
    value: T,
}

fn unwrap_or(opt: OptionValue<i32>, default: i32) -> i32 { ... }

Arithmetic and type contracts (written 2026-10-29)

This section writes several implementation-verified semantic positions as contracts (source: the characterization census of the std improvement batch; the parenthesized numbers are entries in the foundation-gap register, see register entry 19).

Division and remainder: truncation direction (TS-2)

Integer division and remainder are truncation-directed, consistently across all three execution paths: SLA emits sdiv/srem (the arithmetic plan in lowering_rules.zig); the compiled path is LLVM's SDiv/SRem (whose semantics are truncation); the interpreted path is @divTrunc/@rem; constant folding is the same. The sign of the remainder follows the dividend.

The positioning of checked arithmetic (TS-6)

The full set of sa_std's checked arithmetic family is exactly three externs: sa_num_add_checked, sa_num_sub_checked, sa_num_mul_checked (i64 only; see sa_std/num.sai). Their positioning is as the landing point for MIR *WithOverflow rvalues (the Rust inflow compiler surface); the semantics are panic(code) on overflow, with no wraparound; num.sal has corresponding macro mirrors for inlining into generated SA. The SLA layer has no checked syntax, and ordinary operators do not go through this family; the num domain also has no named wrapping / saturating function family. For ordinary operators' own overflow position, see register entry 1; their dual-path alignment belongs to a later batch.

usize / isize are always 64-bit (TS-8)

usize / isize are always 64-bit at the SLA layer, target-independent: the checker's size table fixes them at 8 bytes, both codegens map them uniformly to SA's u64 / i64, and the plugin has no target bit-width switch and no wasm32 branch. Therefore usize arithmetic in wasm artifacts is also 64-bit; there is no "native 64-bit vs wasm 32-bit" divergence; the position is that the usize bit width is decoupled from the host pointer width. (The host bridge surface that passes pointers through JS numbers belongs to the SAX / airlock layer and is outside this position.)

char: SLA has no such type (main register entry 3)

The SLA language layer has no char type: the Primitive enum has no char, and neither the lexicon nor the syntax has character literals. char exists only at the SA / std layer: sa_std/char.sal defines CHAR_SIZE = 4 and CHAR_MAX = 1114111 (0x10FFFF) and excludes the surrogate range (55296–57343) — i.e. a macro library of u32-wide Unicode scalar values (synonymous with Rust's char); sa_std/char.sa has the CHAR_IS_VALID_SCALAR / CHAR_FROM_U32 validation macros.

To be verifiedThe behavioral position for over-wide shifts (shift amount ≥ bit width) has not yet been written: the source forms of the three execution paths differ from each other, and it will be pinned down after box-probe verification (register TS-3).
